tools.description: How many independent bets a set of return series holds: the participation ratio of their weekly correlations (n for unrelated series, 1 for copies), and with families, the families' bets and the ideas they cluster into.

tools.name: annotation_packet
tools.title: Annotation packets
tools.description: Start a labelled dataset: figures (company, measure, period, value) are checked by machine against the SEC filings and written as blind CSV packets for two or more people to label, with guidelines and a key holding the machine labels.

tools.name: annotation_agreement
tools.title: Annotation agreement
tools.description: Read filled annotation packets: how often the people agree (Cohen's kappa), how often they agree with the machine, and every disagreement.

tools.name: annotation_gold
tools.title: Annotation gold set
tools.description: Merge filled annotation packets and a reviewer's decisions into a gold dataset (JSONL: each item's label, who decided it, the machine label and source) with a datasheet of agreement and hashes.

tools.name: enforcement_actions
tools.title: SEC enforcement actions
tools.description: The SEC's latest enforcement: litigation releases and administrative proceedings, with who was named, the number and the document, across the market or filtered to a company or person (every word of the name must match). The feeds hold the latest actions only, so an empty answer is limited to what they reach.

tools.name: consumer_complaints
tools.title: Consumer complaints (CFPB)
tools.description: Complaints consumers sent the CFPB about a bank, lender, card issuer or credit bureau: totals, the last 12 months, top products and issues, and how often the company answered in time. Complaints are unverified and not adjusted for size.

tools.name: product_recalls
tools.title: Product recalls (FDA, NHTSA)
tools.description: Recalls: a firm's FDA recalls of drugs, devices and food with class, reason and status, and a vehicle's NHTSA safety recalls by make, model and year.

tools.name: sanctions_check
tools.title: Sanctions list (OFAC SDN)
tools.description: Search the U.S. Treasury's Specially Designated Nationals list and its aliases for a person, company, bank or vessel, by whole words. Not a compliance screening: no match is not clearance, and a match needs checking against the entry.

tools.name: federal_rules
tools.title: Federal Register rules
tools.description: Federal Register documents: final and proposed rules, notices and presidential documents by words and agency (SEC, CFTC, Fed, Treasury, CFPB, FDA and more), with comment deadlines, effective dates and abstracts. Can list only rules still open for comment.

tools.name: technical_indicators
tools.title: Technical indicators
tools.description: The common technical indicators for a symbol in one call, from its daily prices: moving averages (SMA and EMA), RSI, MACD, Bollinger Bands and ATR, with where the close sits against its 50- and 200-day averages. Standard definitions; describes past prices, not a forecast.

tools.name: stock_snapshot
tools.title: Analyst targets, valuation and short interest
tools.description: What a quote page shows and no primary source publishes, from Yahoo Finance: analysts' mean, median, high and low price targets, how many analysts, the recommendation and ratings, EPS and revenue estimates by quarter and year, market cap, trailing and forward P/E and other ratios, 52-week range, dividend rate, short interest, institutional and insider percentages, next earnings date. Vendor aggregates, labeled as such; for reported figures use the filings.

tools.name: security_identifiers
tools.title: Security identifiers (OpenFIGI)
tools.description: Map a ticker, ISIN, CUSIP, SEDOL or FIGI to one security through OpenFIGI: its name, FIGIs, listings, exchange and type. Check digits are tested first, so a mistyped ISIN or CUSIP is refused.

tools.name: legal_entity
tools.title: Legal entity (LEI)
tools.description: Who a company legally is, from the Global LEI register: legal name, LEI, jurisdiction, status, addresses, former names, its direct and ultimate parents and how many entities it owns. By name or LEI; works for firms worldwide, listed or not.

tools.name: world_yields
tools.title: World government yields
tools.description: Government bond yields side by side: U.S. Treasury, euro area (ECB, AAA), UK (Bank of England), Japan (Ministry of Finance) and Canada (Bank of Canada), by maturity, with the date and basis of each curve, 10Y-2Y slopes and 10-year spreads to the U.S.

tools.name: credit_cycle
tools.title: Credit cycle (BIS)
tools.description: The BIS credit cycle by country: private credit as a share of GDP, its long-run trend and the credit-to-GDP gap, an early-warning measure regulators use for banking stress. Up to 40 quarters.

tools.name: dividend_history
tools.title: Dividend history
tools.description: A security's dividends and splits: each payment by ex-date, totals by year, the trailing 12-month yield, five-year growth and the streak of rising annual totals. Works for foreign listings.

tools.name: verify_claims
tools.title: Verify claims against filings
tools.description: Check a draft answer's figures against the company's own filings before using them: revenue, net income, EPS, operating income, margins, growth, cash flow, assets, debt and more, for a fiscal year or quarter as the company labels it. US and foreign filers (20-F, IFRS), in their own currency. Each claim comes back confirmed, contradicted (with the filed figure and what the claimed one matches instead: another year, a quarter, a unit slip), not reported or not checkable.

tools.name: exposure_map
tools.title: Who depends on this company
tools.description: Who depends on a company, from what others say in their annual reports: every filer that names it, with the passage, and whether it reads as a supplier, customer or competitor. For supply chains no fund report shows. Read by rules, so check the passage.

tools.name: guidance_record
tools.title: Management's record against its own guidance
tools.description: A management team's record against its own word: each quarter it gave guidance in its press release, what it said and what then happened, how often results came in above, within and below its own range, and which quarters fell short.

tools.name: what_happened_next
tools.title: What happened next, every past time
tools.description: Every past time a market or stock fell, rose or sat this far below its high: each case, what followed a month, a quarter and a year later, the worst and best, and how that compares with an ordinary day. A record, not a forecast or advice.

tools.name: filing_memory
tools.title: Search all of a company's annual reports
tools.description: Everything one company has said about a subject across every annual report it has on EDGAR, back to the 1990s where they exist: the best passages with links, how often it came up each year, and optionally how that moved with a margin, tested against chance. Reads the reports on this machine; no key. Supply the company's likely words in also and all_of, since a company rarely uses yours.

tools.name: filing_sentiment
tools.title: Filing tone (local FinBERT)
tools.description: The tone of a filing or any text, sentence by sentence, from FinBERT run on this machine: an 8-K's press release by default, or a 10-K section. Needs the optional local models (canli-mcp models install). Tone, not truth, and no evidence it predicts a price; the model is licensed for non-commercial use.

tools.name: shipping_activity
tools.title: Shipping activity (IMF PortWatch)
tools.description: Ships moving through the world's straits and canals (Suez, Panama, Malacca, Hormuz and others) and ports, from the IMF's PortWatch, which estimates them from satellite tracking of ships. All chokepoints against a year ago, one chokepoint by week, or one port. No key.

tools.name: page_attention
tools.title: Public attention (Wikipedia)
tools.description: Daily Wikipedia page views for a company or subject: a plain measure of public attention, with how the last week compares with normal. No key.

tools.name: latest_price
tools.title: Latest price
tools.description: The latest price of a stock, ETF, index, currency or crypto pair, with the previous close and the time of the price. No key; can run late, by 15 minutes or more on some markets.

tools.name: european_filings
tools.title: European filings (ESEF)
tools.description: A European company's annual financial report as it filed it in the European Single Electronic Format (ESEF): revenue, operating and net profit, EPS, assets, equity, cash, cash flows and dividends as the company tagged them (IFRS concepts, its currency, full scale), with the comparatives, the report's viewer link and the other years on file. Issuers on EU and EEA regulated markets, found by name or LEI; words find any other tagged figure.

tools.name: reference_rates
tools.title: Reference and policy rates
tools.description: Money-market and policy rates and the ECB's euro exchange reference rates (fx:GBP) from the central banks themselves: SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, EFFR and OBFR from the New York Fed (with percentiles and volume), the euro short-term rate and the ECB's policy rates, SONIA and Bank Rate from the Bank of England, and about forty central banks' policy rates as the BIS collects them (policy:JP, policy:Brazil). Dates and rates, oldest first.

tools.name: prediction_markets
tools.title: Prediction markets
tools.description: What traders on Polymarket and Kalshi are paying for an outcome, found by words (a Fed decision, a recession, an election, a price level): each market's probability (the middle of bid and ask, else the last trade), bid, ask, volume and closing date, with the event's resolution rules.

tools.name: crypto_fundamentals
tools.title: Crypto fundamentals (DefiLlama)
tools.description: A DeFi protocol's total value locked (now, by chain, and its history), the fees users pay it and the revenue it keeps (24 hours to all time); a chain's total value locked; or a stablecoin's supply in circulation and its change, by chain. From DefiLlama's open data.

tools.name: financial_statements
tools.title: Financial statements as filed
tools.description: A company's financial statements exactly as filed: income statement, balance sheet, cash flow and equity statement from its 10-K (or 10-Q), with its own line labels, each line's XBRL concept and the values as the filing shows them (units say the scale). Joins several filings by period; a line a later filing restated, or that a stock split changed, is shown beside its first-reported figure, never mixed in.

tools.name: filing_tables
tools.title: Tables in filings
tools.description: The table in a filing that holds a figure, found by words ("paid members", "revenue by region", "guidance"): XBRL statement and detail reports and the tables in the document itself (MD&A figures such as members, stores or ARPU), or an 8-K press release's tables. With filings above one, the same words in each earlier filing, to follow a figure over the years. Without words, lists the tables.

tools.name: earnings_release
tools.title: Earnings release and guidance
tools.description: A quarter's results press release (8-K Item 2.02): the headline, the results it states (each with the part of the business it belongs to and what a change is measured against), its guidance parsed into ranges (low, high, midpoint, unit, measure, basis, period, and the sentence or table row), and the previous release's guidance for this quarter set against the company's results: above, within or below the range, in basis points for rates.

tools.name: release_check
tools.title: Earnings release against the 10-Q or 10-K
tools.description: A quarter's results press release set against the 10-Q or 10-K filed after it: every figure in the release's tables looked for among the report's inline XBRL facts for the same period. Lists the figures that changed (release value, filed value, difference, percent, the XBRL concept and how the line was matched), release figures with no counterpart (non-GAAP measures, metrics) and lines the report adds, such as a charge booked after the release.

tools.name: audit_signals
tools.title: Going-concern doubts, auditor changes and critical audit matters
tools.description: What auditors and companies say when something is wrong, from SEC filings. Going-concern doubt: each 10-K and 10-Q whose text says there is substantial doubt about the company's ability to continue, as a timeline (first raised, still raised, lifted), or across the market the companies whose latest report newly raised it. Auditor changes (8-K Item 4.01): who left and who came, resigned or dismissed, disagreements and reportable events. The latest 10-K's critical audit matters. Each row quotes the filing.

tools.name: screen_companies
tools.title: Screen companies
tools.description: Screen every US-listed company (thousands, from SEC XBRL frames) on fundamentals: revenue, growth, margins, ROE, ROA, free cash flow, R&D intensity, leverage and more, for a calendar year or each company's fiscal year ending in a date window, with filters, ranking and optional valuation (price, market cap, P/E, P/S, FCF yield). Implausible figures (tagging slips) are held out and listed apart.

tools.name: company_report
tools.title: Company report
tools.description: One company in one call: profile, five fiscal years of financials (revenue, growth, margins, net income, EPS, cash flow, ROE, leverage), price and risk over a year (return, volatility, drawdown, beta), valuation (market cap, P/E, P/S, FCF yield), insider buying and selling, and recent filings, each from its source.

tools.name: event_study
tools.title: Event study
tools.description: How a stock's price reacted to events: earnings releases (8-K item 2.02), insider purchases or sales (Form 4), any 8-K, or given dates. Abnormal returns against a market model, cumulative abnormal return per event and on average, with a t test across events. For filings use event_type (with last for the most recent few), not filing dates: it starts day 0 at the first session after the SEC accepted the filing.

tools.name: mentions_trend
tools.title: Mentions over time
tools.description: How often a word or phrase appears in SEC filings over time (by month, quarter or year), across all filers or one company, from EDGAR full-text search: for themes such as "tariffs", "agentic AI" or "going concern".

tools.name: company_profile
tools.title: Company profile
tools.description: A company's or fund's SEC profile by ticker, CIK or name: tickers, exchange, industry (SIC), fiscal year end, state, address, former names, and its latest 10-K, 10-Q, 8-K and 13F.

tools.name: list_filings
tools.title: List filings
tools.description: A company's SEC filings, newest first, filtered by form type (10-K, 10-Q, 8-K, DEF 14A, S-1, 4, 13F-HR...) and dates, with links. Use read_filing to read one.

tools.name: read_filing
tools.title: Read a filing
tools.description: The text of an SEC filing: the latest of a form, or one by accession. For a 10-K or 10-Q, section returns one item ("risk factors", "md&a", "business", "market risk", "legal proceedings", or a number such as "1A"); without it the result lists the items and their lengths. document reads an exhibit, such as an 8-K's press release ("EX-99.1"). find returns only the passages with given words ("employees", "buyback"), the fastest way to a fact in a long filing; otherwise long text pages with offset.

tools.name: search_filings
tools.title: Search filings
tools.description: Full-text search across all SEC filings since 2001 (EDGAR full-text search): which companies mention a phrase, filtered by form, filer and dates. Quote phrases.

tools.name: insider_trades
tools.title: Insider trades
tools.description: Insider transactions at a company from its Form 4 filings: who (officers, directors, 10% owners), what (open-market buys and sales, option exercises, tax withholding, gifts), shares, price, value, holdings after, and 10b5-1 plan flags, with a buy/sell summary. Default: the last 90 days.

tools.name: fund_holdings
tools.title: Fund holdings (13F)
tools.description: A fund manager's 13F holdings for a quarter (latest by default): positions by value with portfolio weights, the total checked against the filing's cover page, and what changed since the previous quarter (new, exited, added, reduced).

tools.name: unusual_options
tools.title: Unusual options activity (Cboe)
tools.description: Unusual options activity for a stock, ETF or index from Cboe's delayed quotes: contracts trading at least as many times their open interest as asked (new positions more likely than closing), ranked by the premium that changed hands, with strike, expiry, IV and delta, and the day's call and put premium.

tools.name: company_emissions
tools.title: Company emissions (EPA greenhouse-gas reports)
tools.description: A company's greenhouse-gas emissions from its US facilities as they reported them to EPA (the Greenhouse Gas Reporting Program): direct emissions in tonnes of CO2e, the company's ownership share of them, by gas, the largest facilities, and a trend over up to five years. Scope 1 from the measurements, not a vendor's ESG score.

tools.name: crypto_markets
tools.title: Crypto markets (CoinGecko)
tools.description: The crypto market from CoinGecko: coins ranked by market value with price, volume, change over a day, a week and a month, supply and distance from the all-time high, and the whole market's value with bitcoin's and ether's shares; or the coins named, by symbol or CoinGecko id.

tools.name: etf_profile
tools.title: ETF or fund profile: costs and holdings
tools.description: What an ETF or mutual fund costs and holds, from Yahoo Finance's fund profile: the expense ratio beside its category's average, turnover, total assets, yield, year-to-date and five-year returns, beta, inception, top holdings with weights, the mix of stocks, bonds and cash, and sector weights.

tools.name: market_calendar
tools.title: Market calendar: earnings, dividends, splits (Nasdaq)
tools.description: The whole market's schedule from Nasdaq's public calendars: who reports earnings on given days (before the open or after the close, consensus EPS and number of estimates, last year's EPS), who goes ex-dividend (amount, record and payment dates), stock splits coming up, and a month's IPOs (priced, expected, filed, withdrawn); filter by tickers or market value.

tools.name: congress_trades
tools.title: Congress trades (House transaction reports)
tools.description: Stock and bond trades by members of the House, read from their periodic transaction reports on the Clerk's site: owner (self, spouse, joint, child), asset and ticker, purchase or sale, trade date, date notified and the amount range, for one member, a state or district, a ticker, or the newest reports filed, with each report's link.

tools.name: analyst_history
tools.title: Analyst rating changes, surprises and revisions
tools.description: A stock's analyst history from Yahoo Finance: every upgrade, downgrade, initiation and target change by firm over any window, the last four quarters' earnings surprises, how the EPS estimate moved over 90 days with the analysts revising it up and down, and the rating counts month by month. stock_snapshot has today's targets and estimates. A vendor's aggregates, labeled so.

tools.name: market_movers
tools.title: Market movers (gainers, losers, most active)
tools.description: Today's biggest US stock gainers, losers and most traded (price, change, volume, average volume, market value), or Yahoo Finance's other ready-made lists: small-cap gainers, most shorted, undervalued growth, growth technology, aggressive small caps, undervalued large caps.

tools.name: market_hours
tools.title: Market hours and holidays (NYSE, Nasdaq)
tools.description: The US stock market's calendar (NYSE and Nasdaq): open, pre-market, after-hours or closed now, the next open and close in Eastern time and UTC, a year's holidays and 1 p.m. early closes, whether a date trades, and how many trading days lie between two dates. Computed from NYSE's rules and its unscheduled closures since 2000, with no network.

tools.name: factor_returns
tools.title: Fama-French factors
tools.description: The Fama-French factors from Kenneth French's data library at Dartmouth: the market over the T-bill (Mkt-RF), size (SMB), value (HML), profitability (RMW), investment (CMA) and momentum (Mom), with the one-month T-bill rate (RF), monthly since 1926, daily or by year, as fractions ready for a factor regression.

tools.name: scenario_risk
tools.title: Portfolio scenarios: macro shocks and past crises
tools.description: A portfolio's holdings under a macro shock or a past crisis. Shock some of eight factors (US stocks, the 2- and 10-year Treasury yields, the Baa-Aaa spread, oil, the dollar, gold, the VIX) and the rest move as history says they do alongside, with a 90% range; or replay a crisis (2008, 2020, 2022 and eight more) beside each holding's actual return then, with the model's error. Betas from weekly returns over the last years. Local server (prices).

tools.name: trade_ticks
tools.title: Crypto trades, tick by tick
tools.description: Every trade on Kraken's public market for a crypto pair (BTC/USD, ETH/EUR, SOL/USD) from any moment back to the market's opening, tick by tick: time to the microsecond, price, size, which side took liquidity and the order type, with the VWAP, buying against selling, the largest trades and one-minute bars built from the ticks. Up to 10,000 trades a call; next_since reads on exactly where it stopped. No key.

tools.name: trade_flows
tools.title: Trade between countries by product
tools.description: What countries buy from and sell to each other, by product, from UN Comtrade: who supplies a country's chips, oil or soybeans and with what share, or how one partner's share moved year by year (in US dollars and kilograms). Products by HS code or plain words. Names Taiwan (listed as Other Asia, nes) and says how much of a total names no partner, which customs offices sometimes withhold. Goods, customs figures a year or two behind. No key.

tools.name: standardized_financials
tools.title: Financials in one template across US GAAP and IFRS
tools.description: A company's income statement, balance sheet and cash flow in one template whether it files US GAAP or IFRS, 26 lines with 14 ratios, each figure saying which tag it came from or the arithmetic that made it. One company over up to 10 fiscal years, or up to five side by side (Apple beside TSMC beside SAP), optionally in US dollars at each year's average and year-end rates. From annual reports at SEC, restatements applied.

tools.name: bond_offerings
tools.title: Bonds a company sold
tools.description: The bonds a company sold, tranche by tranche, from the SEC filings that priced them: amount, coupon, maturity, price, yield, spread over Treasuries (mid-swaps for euro bonds, the index for floating notes), benchmark and CUSIP from each final term sheet, with the XBRL fee tables of final prospectuses confirming amounts and adding deals priced without one. Each dollar yield is recomputed from its price. Yearly totals by currency. Registered deals only.

tools.name: financial_cycle
tools.title: House prices, debt service, credit and exchange rates by country
tools.description: Where countries stand in their financial cycle, from the Bank for International Settlements: house prices (real and nominal, with the change on a year), the share of income households and companies spend servicing debt, credit to households, companies and government as a share of GDP, and real and nominal effective exchange rates. Up to eight countries side by side, 40 to 60 economies covered, with history. No key.

tools.name: treasury_cash
tools.title: Treasury cash (Daily Treasury Statement)
tools.description: The Treasury's cash at the Fed each business day since 2005 (the Treasury General Account, from the Daily Treasury Statement), its change and range over the window, and optionally the last day's largest deposits and withdrawals by category (taxes withheld, debt issued and redeemed, interest, Social Security) with month and fiscal year to date.

tools.name: fed_liquidity
tools.title: Fed liquidity: repo facilities, holdings, reserves
tools.description: The Fed's footprint in the money markets: the overnight reverse repo facility's daily take-up and the standing repo facility's lending (New York Fed, its test trades kept apart), the Fed's securities holdings week by week with the pace they change by type, and its balance sheet: total assets, reserve balances, the TGA and net liquidity (assets less the TGA and the reverse repo). Each with changes over a week, four weeks and a year, a plain summary first; or any of them day by day or week by week. No key.

tools.name: money_markets
tools.title: Money markets: repo, money funds and dealers
tools.description: The US money markets' plumbing, no key: overnight repo by segment (SOFR, TGCR, BGCR, tri-party without the Fed, GCF, cleared bilateral DVP), each rate with its volume and its spread to the Fed's interest on reserves and overnight reverse repo rate; what US money market funds hold by type and whom their repo is with (Form N-MFP, via the OFR); and primary dealers' net Treasury positions by maturity (New York Fed). part gives one with its history.

tools.name: inflation_nowcast
tools.title: Inflation nowcast (Cleveland Fed)
tools.description: The Cleveland Fed's daily nowcast of inflation not yet published: its estimate of CPI, core CPI, PCE and core PCE for the coming months and the quarter, on the month, on a year and annualized, beside the last month published. month gives one month's nowcast day by day and its figure once out; record sets the last nowcast before each release against the published figure, with the average miss. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: rate_expectations
tools.title: Fed rate odds from futures (FedWatch method)
tools.description: What the futures market expects the Fed to do: from 30-day fed funds futures, the rate implied after each scheduled FOMC meeting, the expected change there and from today, the chances of no change, a hike or a cut, and of each target range after each meeting, by the method CME's FedWatch publishes, with the contracts behind it and today's range and effective rate. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: job_postings
tools.title: Job postings (Indeed Hiring Lab)
tools.description: Labour demand as Indeed sees it, day by day: job postings against 1 February 2020 (= 100), seasonally adjusted, in the US, Canada, the UK, Australia, Germany, France, Ireland, Italy, Spain, the Netherlands and the euro area, with the change over four weeks, a quarter and a year and the distance from the peak; by occupational sector or by state, province or region, ranked; or every economy side by side. Indeed Hiring Lab data (CC BY 4.0). No key.

tools.name: reserve_currencies
tools.title: Currencies of the world's reserves (IMF COFER)
tools.description: What the world's central banks hold their foreign exchange reserves in, from the IMF's COFER: each currency's share of the reserves whose currency is reported (the dollar, euro, yen, sterling, renminbi and others) and its value in dollars at the latest quarter, the change in share on a year and over ten years, and the shares quarter by quarter. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: housing_market
tools.title: US housing market (Zillow, Realtor.com)
tools.description: The US housing market, nationally or for a metro area: Zillow's typical home value with its change on a month, a year and five years and its distance from the peak; Realtor.com's listings (median listing price, active and new listings, days on market, the share with a price cut, pending sales), each against a year earlier; and the 30-year mortgage rate. rank lists the largest metros by how fast home values rise or fall. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: gdp_nowcast
tools.title: GDP nowcast (Atlanta Fed GDPNow)
tools.description: The Atlanta Fed's GDPNow, its running estimate of real GDP before the BEA publishes it (annualized): the latest nowcast and each update since the first with the data releases behind it, what each part of spending adds and each part's own pace, the BEA's latest estimates beside it, and the model's record against the BEA's advance estimates. Read from the Atlanta Fed's workbook. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: consumer_expectations
tools.title: Consumer expectations (New York Fed survey)
tools.description: What American households expect, from the New York Fed's Survey of Consumer Expectations, monthly: inflation over one, three and five years, home prices, the prices of gas, food, rent, medical care and college, earnings, income and spending, and the chances of losing or finding a job, of higher unemployment, of missing a debt payment and of stocks rising; the latest month beside a month and a year before, or one topic month by month. No key.

tools.name: margin_debt
tools.title: Margin debt (FINRA)
tools.description: How much investors borrow against their stocks, from FINRA's monthly margin statistics since 1997: margin debt (customers' debit balances at member firms) with its change on a month and a year, the record and how far the latest is from it, the free credit balances in cash and margin accounts, and the months before. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: options_sentiment
tools.title: Options sentiment: put/call ratios (Cboe)
tools.description: How much protection options traders buy, from Cboe's daily market statistics: the total, equity, index, ETF, VIX and SPX put/call ratios of the latest trading day with the calls and puts traded, and the total, equity, index and SPX ratios day by day with their 10- and 20-day averages. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: recession_watch
tools.title: Recession indicators against their lines
tools.description: The indicators read for a US recession, each beside the line it is read against and whether it is past it: the New York Fed's yield-curve model (the chance of being in recession twelve months ahead, computed as the New York Fed publishes it, month by month), the Sahm rule, the 10-year less 2-year curve and its last inversion, jobless claims against a year earlier, the Chauvet-Piger probability, GDPNow, and the Fed Board staff's excess bond premium model. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: state_economy
tools.title: US state economies (BLS, FHFA, BEA, Philadelphia Fed)
tools.description: A US state's economy beside the nation's: the unemployment rate, payroll jobs, the Philadelphia Fed's coincident index of activity, house prices (FHFA) and real GDP, each with its change on a year; or every state and DC ranked by unemployment or by the growth of jobs, activity or house prices. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: inflation_breakdown
tools.title: CPI by component (BLS)
tools.description: What is driving US consumer prices, from the BLS's CPI: all items and core beside food (at home and away), energy and gasoline, core goods and used cars, core services, shelter, rent, owners' equivalent rent, medical care and transportation services, each on the month (seasonally adjusted), over three months at an annual rate and on a year as the BLS states it, with the headline and core month by month. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: fed_speeches
tools.title: Fed speeches and releases
tools.description: What the Federal Reserve Board says, from its own feeds: the latest speeches and testimony by its members and its monetary policy releases (statements, minutes), with speaker, title, date, venue and link; one member's; or one speech read, its paragraphs on monetary policy and the economy quoted as given. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: central_bank_speeches
tools.title: Central bankers' speeches (BIS)
tools.description: What central bankers everywhere are saying, from the BIS's collection of their speeches: the latest fifty with speaker, role and bank, title, date and link; one bank's (ECB, Bank of England, Bundesbank, Bank of Japan...) or one speaker's; or one speech read, brief excerpts of its passages on policy. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: financial_conditions
tools.title: Financial conditions and market stress
tools.description: How loose or tight US financial conditions are and how much stress markets show, in one answer: the OFR's daily Financial Stress Index with what credit, equity valuation, safe assets, funding and volatility each add; the Chicago Fed's NFCI and its parts; the St. Louis and Kansas City Feds' stress indexes; corporate bond spreads by rating (ICE BofA), Moody's Baa spread and the Fed Board's excess bond premium; the VIX. Each with its changes and its place in its own history.

tools.name: market_breadth
tools.title: Market breadth: how many members take part
tools.description: How many of an index's members take part in its moves, computed from the members themselves: the share of the S&P 500's (or the S&P 400's, the Dow's, or one sector's) members above their 50- and 200-day averages, how many rose and fell, new 52-week highs and lows, how far the typical member is below its high, the average member's return beside the index's own over a day, a month, the year to date and a year, recent sessions' breadth, and by_sector for the eleven sectors.

tools.name: labor_market
tools.title: US jobs report in one answer
tools.description: The US jobs picture in one answer: payroll gains with the three-month average, the unemployment rate and U-6, participation and the prime-age employment ratio, wages and hours, JOLTS openings, quits and layoffs with openings per unemployed person, and weekly jobless claims, each beside the reading before and a year before, with payroll gains month by month. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: commodity_prices
tools.title: Commodity prices (World Bank Pink Sheet)
tools.description: World commodity prices from the World Bank's Pink Sheet, monthly since 1960: oil, gas, LNG and coal, metals and precious metals, grains, oilseeds, coffee, cocoa, sugar, cotton, rubber, timber and fertilizers, each with its change on a month, a year and five years, beside the World Bank's sector indexes; or one commodity month by month with its record; all for every commodity. A plain summary first. No key.

tools.name: federal_budget
tools.title: Federal budget (Monthly Treasury Statement)
tools.description: The US federal budget month by month from the Monthly Treasury Statement (since 2015): receipts, outlays and the deficit for this fiscal year and the last, and the fiscal year to date against the same months a year earlier, for the latest statement or any month's.

tools.name: crypto_options
tools.title: Crypto options (Deribit)
tools.description: Crypto options from Deribit's public data: each expiry's at-the-money implied volatility, call and put open interest, put/call ratio and the day's volume, with DVOL (Deribit's 30-day implied volatility index) for BTC and ETH; or one expiry's chain, strike by strike, with bids, asks and implied volatilities in US dollars. BTC, ETH, SOL, XRP and others.

tools.name: treasury_yields
tools.title: Treasury yields
tools.description: US Treasury daily yields from the Treasury itself: the par yield curve (1 month to 30 years), real (TIPS) yields or bill rates, for the latest day, a date, or a date range. In percent.

tools.name: economic_series
tools.title: Economic series (FRED)
tools.description: Any FRED economic series (inflation, unemployment, GDP, payrolls, rates, credit spreads, oil, FX, money supply, recession indicators) by id or plain words, as dates and values, optionally as changes or year-over-year rates. as_of reads it as published on a past date (ALFRED vintages: before later revisions), and revisions shows each value then against now. Feed values straight into analysis tools.

tools.name: price_history
tools.title: Price history
tools.description: Price bars (open, high, low, close, volume), monthly to one-minute, for US stocks and ETFs, stocks listed abroad (SAP.DE, 7203.T), currency pairs (EUR/USD), futures (crude oil, gold), indices and yields (S&P 500, VIX, 10 year yield) and crypto (bitcoin), by symbol or plain name. Stocks adjust for splits and dividends by default, with dividends, splits and the total return; returns: true adds daily returns. No key needed; uses the user's Alpaca or Tiingo key for US stocks when set.

tools.name: fund_portfolio
tools.title: Fund or ETF portfolio (N-PORT)
tools.description: What a US mutual fund or ETF holds, from its own SEC Form N-PORT (VOO, IVV, QQQ, AGG, FXAIX): every position with value and weight, exposure by asset type, issuer, country and currency, a bond fund's coupon and maturity profile, its monthly returns, the money that came in and went out each month, and what changed since the previous quarter.

tools.name: options_chain
tools.title: Options chain (Cboe)
tools.description: An option chain from Cboe's delayed data for a stock, ETF or index (AAPL, SPY, SPX, VIX): bids, asks, implied volatility, greeks, open interest and volume by strike for one expiration, every expiration with its open interest, put/call ratios, max pain and the move the at-the-money straddle prices in.

tools.name: volatility_surface
tools.title: Volatility surface (Cboe)
tools.description: The implied volatility surface from Cboe's delayed option data: at-the-money IV by expiration (term structure), 25-delta put and call IV with the risk reversal and butterfly (skew), and IV at fixed moneyness from 80 to 120 percent of the price (smile).

tools.name: futures_curve
tools.title: Futures curve (Cboe)
tools.description: A Cboe futures curve from its daily settlements: VIX futures by expiration with the VIX index, contango or backwardation and the front month's premium; also mini VIX, variance, bitcoin and iBoxx bond index futures.

tools.name: figure_trace
tools.title: figure_trace
tools.description: How a reported figure is built, from the filing itself: the lines the company's own XBRL calculation adds up to it, each line's value, every sum recomputed and checked, what the figure feeds into, and how the filing splits it by segment, product or region. It shows the filing agrees with itself, not that the figures are right.

tools.name: filing_check
tools.title: Filing check: the document against its XBRL
tools.description: Every number in a 10-K or 10-Q read twice: as a person reads the document and as machines read its inline XBRL. Lists each figure tagged at a scale other than the unit its table or words state, each fact tagged twice with different values, each sum in the filing's own calculation that does not add up, and each fact SEC's company facts hold differently or not at all, with a link to the figure, and counts of what was checked.

tools.name: source_check
tools.title: Source check: are the documents still the same
tools.description: Whether the documents behind an answer are still the bytes it was read from: give the evidence rows (or a canli-mcp receipt's sources) and each document is read again, past every cache, as the same, changed since, or unreachable. Only documents from the sources this server reads are fetched.

tools.name: token_check
tools.title: token_check
tools.description: What an ERC-20 token's contract can do and how much of it exists, read from the chain: mint, pause, blacklist and upgrade powers, owner, proxy, source verification, supply, and an unlock schedule you give set against it. It names what the code allows. A clean reading never means safe, and it cannot detect a rug pull.

tools.name: segment_revenue
tools.title: Revenue by segment
tools.description: Where a company's revenue comes from, read from the XBRL of its latest 10-K (or 10-Q): revenue and operating income by business segment, revenue by product or service and by region, for up to three years, with the company's own labels and each breakdown checked against total revenue.

tools.name: index_constituents
tools.title: Index constituents
tools.description: The members of a stock index (S&P 500, S&P 400, the Dow, Nasdaq 100, Russell 2000, MSCI EAFE, a Select Sector) with their weights: from the latest day's holdings State Street publishes (SPY, MDY, DIA, the sector SPDRs), or the N-PORT of an ETF that tracks the index, with the date, the number of members and how concentrated the top ten are.

tools.name: fomc
tools.title: Fed rate decisions (FOMC)
tools.description: The Federal Reserve's rate decisions from its own record: each FOMC meeting of a year (held and scheduled), the action, change and target range, the vote with dissenters and their reasons, links to statements and minutes, the latest statement, and the median projections (dot plot) for GDP, unemployment, inflation and the federal funds rate.

tools.name: economic_calendar
tools.title: Economic calendar
tools.description: The US economic calendar from the agencies' own schedules: when BLS (jobs, CPI, PPI, JOLTS), BEA (GDP, personal income and PCE, trade), the Census Bureau (retail sales, housing starts, durable goods) and the Fed (FOMC decisions) release, with times in US Eastern and the market-moving releases flagged.

tools.name: executive_pay
tools.title: Executive pay vs performance
tools.description: What a company's executives are paid against how it did, from the pay-versus-performance table in its proxy: the CEO's reported pay and the pay actually earned, the other executives' averages, shareholder return against peers, net income and the company's chosen measure, five years; or every company's CEO pay ranked, with mis-scaled filings held out.

tools.name: short_interest
tools.title: Short interest (FINRA)
tools.description: Short interest in US stocks from FINRA, twice a month: shares short, the change, average daily volume and days to cover over several reports, and the share of shares outstanding from the company's latest SEC cover page; or, with no stock, the market ranked by days to cover, change or size.

tools.name: off_exchange_volume
tools.title: Dark pool and OTC volume (FINRA)
tools.description: How much of a US stock trades away from the exchanges, from FINRA's OTC transparency data: weekly shares and trades in dark pools (ATSs) and with other off-exchange dealers, and the largest dark pools and dealers in the latest week.

tools.name: fails_to_deliver
tools.title: Fails to deliver (SEC)
tools.description: Shares that failed to settle, from the SEC's fails-to-deliver data (NSCC): a stock's outstanding fail balance on each settlement date over the latest half-month files, with prices and dollar values, or the securities with the largest fails across the market.

tools.name: futures_positioning
tools.title: Futures positioning (CFTC COT)
tools.description: Who holds what in a futures market, from the CFTC's weekly Commitments of Traders: long, short and net positions of producers, swap dealers, managed money and others (or dealers, asset managers and leveraged funds for financial futures), with weekly changes and where the speculators sit in their range, by market name (gold, crude oil, 10 year note, euro, bitcoin).

tools.name: private_offerings
tools.title: Private offerings (Form D)
tools.description: Private markets from Form D, filed when startups and funds sell securities without registering: amount offered and sold, number of investors, minimum investment, exemption (Rule 506(b) or 506(c)), industry, fund type and the people behind it, for one issuer or across the market (newest first, filtered by industry or amount sold).

tools.name: company_events
tools.title: Company events (8-K)
tools.description: Company news from the source: the events companies must report on Form 8-K (earnings, deals, executive changes, restatements, auditor changes, bankruptcies, cyber incidents, layoffs, delisting notices), for one company or, by event, across the whole market, each with the headline of the press release it attached and the opening of what the filing says.

tools.name: latest_filings
tools.title: Latest filings (EDGAR feed)
tools.description: What has just been filed with the SEC, across every company: EDGAR's latest-filings feed, newest first by acceptance time, filtered by form (8-K, 10-K, 4, SC 13D, S-1...), 8-K event (earnings, executive change, restatement, bankruptcy), words in the filer's name and time. For watching what comes in today and over the last few business days; list_filings and company_events reach further back.

tools.name: filing_diff
tools.title: What changed in a filing
tools.description: What changed in a company's 10-K (or 10-Q) against the one before, section by section (risk factors by default, MD&A, business, legal proceedings): new and dropped paragraphs, the sentences changed in the rest, and the words whose use rose or fell most.

tools.name: news
tools.title: News and tone (GDELT)
tools.description: News about a company or a topic from the world's press (the GDELT Project's open index, no key): articles newest first with outlet and country, and the daily average tone of the coverage.

tools.name: explain_move
tools.title: Explain a stock move
tools.description: Why a stock moved on a day, in one call: its return against the market and how rare it was for this stock (a market model fitted on the year before, with a z-score), the company's SEC filings around the day (8-K items named), and the press's headlines from those days.

tools.name: portfolio_xray
tools.title: Portfolio X-ray (look-through)
tools.description: A portfolio seen through its funds: each ETF or mutual fund opened into the positions of its latest SEC N-PORT and added to the stocks held directly, giving the real exposure to each company, the overlap between funds and the effective number of positions.

tools.name: comps
tools.title: Comparable companies
tools.description: A comparable-companies table: the company beside its NYSE- and Nasdaq-listed peers in the same SEC industry code, the nearest in revenue, on revenue, growth, margins, ROE, R&D intensity and FCF margin (or measures you pick), with the peers' median and the company's rank on each.

tools.name: debt_profile
tools.title: Debt profile
tools.description: A company's debt from its annual reports' XBRL: total and net debt, the maturity ladder from the debt note (next 12 months to after five years), lease payments, interest expense, the implied interest rate, interest coverage and debt to EBITDA, with five years of debt and cash.

tools.name: ownership_breadth
tools.title: Breadth of institutional ownership (13F)
tools.description: How many institutions hold a stock, quarter by quarter: 13F filers whose holdings tables list its CUSIP (EDGAR full-text search), with the change and a sample of holders. A fall in breadth predicted lower returns (Chen, Hong and Stein 2002).

tools.name: forensic_scores
tools.title: Forensic accounting screens
tools.description: Three accounting screens in one call from the company's own annual XBRL for its last two years: Beneish's M-score (earnings manipulation), Piotroski's F-score (financial strength) and Altman's Z-score (distress), every input with its tag.

tools.name: funding_rates
tools.title: Crypto funding rates (OKX)
tools.description: Crypto perpetual funding on OKX's USDT perpetuals, no key: each coin's latest eight-hour rate, the window's mean and its annualized carry (short the perpetual against long spot), the last week's, and the share of positive periods.

tools.name: compute_prices
tools.title: GPU compute prices (Cirrun index)
tools.description: Compute as a market, no key: the on-demand hourly price of each data-centre GPU (B200, H200, H100, A100, L40S...) across the clouds and GPU marketplaces, the cheapest, median and dearest offer with who offers it, every provider's offer for one model, recent list-price changes, and the Cirrun GPU Index (a daily chained index of those prices). Each price is the provider's own list price with the date it was confirmed.

tools.name: shareholder_returns
tools.title: Dividends and buybacks
tools.description: What a company has paid its shareholders, year by year from its annual XBRL: dividends per share (split-adjusted record: years raised in a row, 5- and 10-year growth) and in total, buybacks and shares issued for cash, the diluted share count and its change, the payout ratio and the share of free cash flow paid out, and at the last close the dividend yield and shareholder yield.

tools.name: buybacks
tools.title: Share buybacks, authorized and bought
tools.description: A company's share buybacks period by period from its own XBRL (SEC company facts): for each fiscal year or quarter, the cash paid for repurchases, the shares bought and the value recorded for them, the average price, the program's authorized and remaining amounts where tagged, and the change in shares outstanding. Each figure names the filing it came from (accession, form, date); a figure the company does not tag is said to be untagged, not estimated.

tools.name: market_overview
tools.title: Market overview
tools.description: The market at a glance, no key: the S&P 500, Nasdaq, Dow, Russell 2000 and VIX, the eleven S&P sectors (SPDR funds) ranked by the month, Treasury yields from 13 weeks to 30 years, the dollar and major currencies, oil, gas, gold, silver and copper, bitcoin and ether, and the main markets in Europe and Asia, each with its last close and its change over a day, a week, a month, three months, the year to date and a year.

tools.name: federal_contracts
tools.title: Federal contracts (USAspending)
tools.description: What the US government obligated to a company in a fiscal year, no key: the total, by agency and industry code, its recipient entities, and its largest contracts with links, from USAspending.gov.

tools.name: drug_pipeline
tools.title: Drug pipeline and FDA approvals
tools.description: A drug company's pipeline, no key: active clinical trials by phase, the readouts (primary completions) due in the coming months, late-stage trials, and its FDA approvals, from ClinicalTrials.gov and Drugs@FDA.

tools.name: comment_letters
tools.title: SEC comment letters
tools.description: What the SEC's staff questioned in a company's filings and how it answered: comment letters (UPLOAD) and replies (CORRESP) grouped into reviews, with the topics of the newest (non-GAAP, revenue recognition, segments...) and excerpts.

tools.name: company_reverse_dcf
tools.title: Reverse DCF (implied growth)
tools.description: The free-cash-flow growth a share price implies: solves a discounted cash flow model for the growth that reaches the market's enterprise value, from the company's annual XBRL and the last close, with a sensitivity table and the company's own history beside it.

tools.name: bank_financials
tools.title: Bank financials (FDIC call reports)
tools.description: A US bank's condition quarter by quarter from its call reports (FDIC, no key): assets, deposits and the share uninsured, loans and the share noncurrent, equity, earnings, ROA, ROE, net interest margin and capital ratios. With no bank, failures since 1934 and their cost, by year or state.

tools.name: filing_drift
tools.title: Language drift across filings
tools.description: How a 10-K section's language drifts over several years: each year's change from the year before (the Lazy Prices measure), hedging and adverse words, readability, and how much it says about a theme you name and how that wording moves, with flags for the years and themes that moved most.

tools.name: planned_insider_sales
tools.title: Planned insider sales (Form 144)
tools.description: Insiders' planned sales from Form 144, filed before they sell: seller, role, shares, market value, share of the company, approximate sale date, how the shares were acquired and any 10b5-1 plan date, with totals by seller.

tools.name: ipo_pipeline
tools.title: IPO pipeline (S-1, F-1, 424B4)
tools.description: The IPO pipeline from EDGAR: companies that filed or amended a registration (S-1, F-1) in a window, labelled IPO candidate, SPAC, fund or already listed, and offerings priced (424B4) with price, shares and proceeds from the prospectus cover.

tools.name: lockup_calendar
tools.title: IPO lock-up expiries (from the prospectus)
tools.description: When insiders' shares from recent IPOs may be sold, from each company's final prospectus (424B4). Across the market, the lock-ups ending in a window: company, IPO date, length as stated (usually 180 days), the date it counts from and the expiry computed from it, staged releases, early-release triggers (earnings release, share price), shares locked up and shares sold. For one company, its terms quoted and later filings that waive or release them.

tools.name: large_holders
tools.title: Large holders (13D/13G)
tools.description: Who owns more than 5 percent of a company, from Schedules 13D and 13G: each holder's latest stake (shares, percent of class, voting power), whether it is passive (13G) or may seek to influence control (13D, with its stated purpose); or, with no company, the newest 13D stakes across the whole market.

tools.name: earnings_calendar
tools.title: Earnings calendar
tools.description: Earnings dates from the companies' own 8-Ks (Item 2.02, results of operations). For a company: its recent results releases with the quarter each covered and whether it came before the open or after the close (EDGAR's acceptance time), and the next release estimated from the same quarter a year earlier, with a window. Across the market: who is due to report in a window, from when they reported in the same weeks last year, marked once they have. Estimates, not announcements.

tools.name: earnings_move
tools.title: Earnings move: priced against past reactions
tools.description: The move the options market prices for a company's next results beside the moves its shares made after its past ones, no key: the next release estimated from a year earlier, the at-the-money straddle of the first expiration after it (Cboe), the results' own move backed out of the expirations either side, and each of the last eight releases' reaction close to close, with the average and how many moved more than priced now.

tools.name: earnings_season
tools.title: Earnings season: beats, misses and surprises
tools.description: How the S&P 500's reporting season is going, no key: how many of its companies have reported, the share that beat, matched or missed the consensus EPS estimate and the median surprise (Nasdaq's calendar, Zacks' consensus), how the ten largest did, the largest beats and misses, by_sector for the eleven sectors, and who is due in the coming days; symbols gives named companies' results first. Members are SPY's daily holdings; share classes count once.

tools.name: investment_advisers
tools.title: Investment advisers (Form ADV)
tools.description: Investment advisers from the SEC's Form ADV database (IAPD) by name or CRD: matching firms with SEC file numbers, status, whether they report disclosure events, offices and branch counts, then the best match in full: registration and since when, other names and relying advisers, its latest ADV date, and links to its Form ADV and brochures.

tools.name: treasury_holders
tools.title: Foreign holders of US Treasuries (TIC)
tools.description: Who holds US Treasury securities, from the Treasury's TIC system: the major foreign holders by country at the last thirteen month ends, each with its change on a year, share of all foreign holdings and rank, the total and what foreign official institutions hold (bills against notes and bonds); or one country's holdings month by month. No key.

tools.name: crop_outlook
tools.title: Crop supply and demand (USDA WASDE)
tools.description: The USDA's world supply and demand estimates (WASDE) for wheat, corn, coarse grains, rice, cotton, soybeans, soybean meal and soybean oil: beginning stocks, production, imports, use, exports and ending stocks by country for the last two market years and this year's projection, with last month's projection beside it and the revision between them. Any month's report, or every country at once. No key.

tools.name: energy_report
tools.title: US oil and gas inventories (EIA weekly)
tools.description: The week in US oil and gas from the EIA's weekly reports: crude (commercial, Cushing, the SPR), gasoline, distillate, jet fuel and propane stocks with the change on the week and the year and against the five-year average and range for the week; refinery utilization; production, trade and products supplied (demand) over four weeks; natural gas in storage by region against a year ago and the five-year average. by_district adds PADD districts; stock gives one stock week by week. Summary first. No key.

tools.name: world_series
tools.title: A country's economy from its own statistics office and central bank
tools.description: A country's economy from the statistics office or central bank that publishes it: inflation, unemployment, GDP growth, policy rate, 10-year yield, exchange rate, industrial production, retail sales, wages, house prices, the OECD's leading indicator, for 70 countries and the euro area, one or up to 30 side by side (G7, G20, EU), or all of one country's. Any series by its publisher's code (IMF, BIS, ECB, Eurostat, OECD, ONS, Bank of Japan, 17 more). check: true compares a second official publisher.

tools.name: world_economy
tools.title: World economy (World Bank)
tools.description: Any country's or region's economy from the World Bank's World Development Indicators (200+ countries, the euro area, the world, income groups): GDP and growth, inflation, unemployment, government debt and deficits, the current account, trade, reserves, interest rates, population and more, by plain words or indicator code, as a year-by-country table with each country's latest value.

tools.name: economic_outlook
tools.title: Economic outlook (OECD projections)
tools.description: The OECD's projections for the next two years from its Economic Outlook, for 50+ economies, the euro area, the OECD and the world: GDP growth, inflation (harmonised for the euro area), core inflation, unemployment, budget balance, government debt, current account and short- and long-term interest rates, beside its estimates for the two years before.

tools.name: treasury_auctions
tools.title: Treasury auctions
tools.description: US Treasury auction results, or the auctions announced next, from the Treasury itself: bills, notes, bonds, TIPS and FRNs by term ("10-year", "13-week bill"), with the rate each cleared at, coupon, bid-to-cover, size and the shares taken by indirect bidders (foreign and other), direct bidders and primary dealers, plus averages to compare the latest auction with recent ones.

tools.name: federal_debt
tools.title: US federal debt
tools.description: The US federal debt each business day from the Treasury's Debt to the Penny (total, held by the public, intragovernmental) over any window since 1993, its change over the window, and the average interest rate the Treasury pays on each type of security.

tools.name: paper_account
tools.title: Paper account
tools.description: Read your Alpaca paper account: equity, cash, buying power, positions, open orders, the market clock, the kill switch and the local order log's verified head.

tools.name: preview_paper_orders
tools.title: Preview paper orders
tools.description: Check orders against your paper account, live quotes, the market clock, your limits file and the kill switch; when every order passes, return a five-minute confirmation token for exactly these orders.

tools.name: rebalance_to_weights
tools.title: Rebalance to weights
tools.description: Turn target portfolio weights into the whole-share orders that move your paper account there (sells first), check them, and return a confirmation token when all pass.

tools.name: verify_attestation
tools.title: Verify an attestation
tools.description: Check an attestation a pre-trade check or send returned: that it was signed by the trader's keys (Ed25519 and, where present, post-quantum ML-DSA-65; both must hold) and not altered, and, given openings from the trader's commitments file, that committed account figures are what they claim. Offline; reads nothing from Alpaca.

tools.name: send_paper_orders
tools.title: Send paper orders
tools.description: Send previewed orders to your Alpaca paper account with their confirmation token (the kill switch is read again first), or cancel open paper orders by id. Every send is logged, hash-chained.
